name: libfixmath
baseline: software single-precision float arithmetic (add, sub, mul, div) as compiled by avr-gcc for ATmega128 (avr-libc/libgcc soft-float; toolchain version unstated)
workload: Per-call cycle counts (min/avg/max) for Q16.16 fix16_add, fix16_sub, fix16_mul and fix16_div versus the same operation on C float, over generated test cases, on a simulated 8-bit AVR ATmega128 built with -O2 -DFIXMATH_OPTIMIZE_8BIT.
claimed_speedup: Average cycles from results-avr.ods (columns inferred as min/avg/max from benchmarks/interface.c print()): fix16_add 67 vs float add 135 (2.0x faster, derived from page data); fix16_sub 75 vs float sub 135 (1.8x faster, derived from page data). Not faster: fix16_mul 377 vs float mul 140 (2.7x slower, derived); fix16_div 637 vs float div 450 (1.4x slower, derived). The sheet also lists fix16_sqrt 706 and fix16_exp 3240 average cycles against float sqrtf/expf rows of 8 cycles, which are measurement artifacts and not a comparison. The README only states that the FIXMATH_FAST_SIN option 'runs at 159% the speed' of libfixmath's own accurate sine (self-comparison).
compiler_and_flags: avr-gcc -Wall -mmcu=atmega128 -std=gnu11 -O2 -DFIXMATH_OPTIMIZE_8BIT (from benchmarks/Makefile; gcc and avr-libc versions not stated). The Cortex-M3 target uses arm-none-eabi-gcc -mcpu=cortex-m3 -mthumb -O2 under QEMU, but no results file for it is committed.
hardware: Simulated ATmega128 in simulavrxx 1.0rc0 or newer (cycle counts from the simulator); no real hardware, host machine not stated.
tradeoffs: Q16.16 only (range about -32768 to 32767.99998, resolution 1/65536); optional lookup tables cost 32 KB for exp and 80 KB for trigonometry unless FIXMATH_NO_CACHE is defined; overflow checking and rounding are on by default and can be disabled by macros; sin/cos accuracy is about 2.1% (2.3% with the fast option).
caveats: Mixed result from the project's own spreadsheet: fixed point wins only add and subtract (about 2x) and loses multiply and divide to software float on this 8-bit target; the best-case rows are the cherry-picked ones. The float sqrtf and expf rows (8 cycles) are artifacts, so no sqrt or exp comparison is valid. The spreadsheet has no column headers (min/avg/max inferred from benchmark.c and interface.c), carries no toolchain versions, and was last edited 2021-05-01 per its metadata, so numbers may predate later code changes. Fixed point is compared with float only, not with another fixed-point library. A Wikipedia article reportedly gives libfixmath atan2 at 26.3% of floating-point time on a Cortex-M0, but that page was blocked (EGRESS_BLOCKED) and was not verified. README says 'Not actively maintained' although a commit landed 2026-07-13.
